title: Information Technology Act s. 67B — Statutory provision (Information Technology Act s. 67B)

content.overview: Material depicting children in sexually explicit acts, etc., in electronic form under Information Technology Act, 2000 — section 67B. Section 67B creates specific offences concerning material depicting children in sexually explicit acts or conduct and related electronic acts, with the statutory child-protection conditions. The answer must identify the statutory trigger, decision-maker, procedure, safeguards, affected rights and available challenge or defence.

content.study:
Statutory rule
Section 67B creates specific offences concerning material depicting children in sexually explicit acts or conduct and related electronic acts, with the statutory child-protection conditions.

Operative conditions
Identify the statutory ground, competent authority, required authorisation, prescribed procedure and any safeguards before assessing validity. Do not collapse executive power, intermediary duty and criminal liability into one question.

Rights and review
Where State action affects speech, privacy or access to information, identify the statutory source and the constitutional standard applicable to the challenge. Distinguish the existence of power from lawful exercise of that power.

Evidence and procedure
For digital records, apply BSA 2023 s. 63 where applicable. Preserve the original direction, notice, authorisation, logs and response trail because procedural compliance can be material.

Current-law caution
Section 66A is struck down and is not a current offence. Use the exact provision and current rules actually applicable to the date of action.

cases.name: Shreya Singhal v. Union of India
cases.facts: The Court reviewed restrictions on online speech under the Information Technology Act.
cases.issue: Whether IT Act s. 66A impermissibly restricted constitutional speech.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Section 66A was vague and overbroad and violated Article 19(1)(a); it was not saved by Article 19(2).
cases.holding: Section 66A was struck down in its entirety.
cases.relevance: Use only as historical status; do not present s. 66A as a current offence.

cases.name: Anvar P.V. v. P.K. Basheer
cases.facts: The Court examined the statutory method for proving electronic records.
cases.issue: Whether electronic records can be admitted without the applicable certificate route.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Electronic records must satisfy the special statutory proof requirements applicable to computer outputs.
cases.holding: The Court reaffirmed the certificate discipline for electronic evidence.
cases.relevance: Use with BSA s. 63 and digital-record admissibility.

cases.name: K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India
cases.facts: The Constitution Bench considered privacy as a constitutional right in the digital and modern State.
cases.issue: Whether privacy is protected as a Fundamental Right.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Privacy is intrinsic to dignity, liberty and Part III, subject to legality, legitimate aim, proportionality and procedural safeguards.
cases.relevance: Use for surveillance, data protection and informational privacy.

I. ISSUE AND JURISDICTION
Whether Information Technology Act s. 67B — Statutory provision (Information Technology Act s. 67B) applies to the stated facts and whether the chosen forum and remedy are maintainable.

II. GOVERNING RULE
Information Technology Act s. 67B — Statutory provision (Information Technology Act s. 67B) is governed by Information Technology Act, 2000, allied rules, the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 where applicable, BSA 2023 and constitutional privacy principles. identify the date, technology, applicable IT Act provision, data regime, intermediary rule and evidence law; distinguish struck-down provisions from current offences.

III. INGREDIENT APPLICATION
Identify each condition, connect it to the evidence and answer the principal exception or defence. Apply BSA s. 63 to digital records where relevant and state the initial burden precisely.

IV. CONCLUSION
Grant, refuse or modify the relief only to the extent authorised by the governing law and proved record.

I. STATEMENT OF FACTS AND PROCEDURAL PROVENANCE
Set out the material facts, forum, procedural stage, notices, pleadings and documents.

II. STATUTORY AND DOCTRINAL SCHEME
Deconstruct Information Technology Act s. 67B — Statutory provision (Information Technology Act s. 67B) under Information Technology Act, 2000, allied rules, the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 where applicable, BSA 2023 and constitutional privacy principles, including its purpose, conditions, exceptions and connected provisions.

III. SATISFACTION OF MANDATORY INGREDIENTS
Apply each ingredient to the record, address jurisdiction, limitation, maintainability and the opposing party's strongest objection.

IV. VERIFIED AUTHORITIES
Use the case ratios below only for the propositions they decide and distinguish contrary facts.

V. EVIDENCE AND PRAYER
Address BSA ss. 63, 104 and 109 where relevant, then seek the precise order available from the designated cyber-crime police and criminal court, adjudicating officer, civil court, High Court under Articles 226/227, or competent data-protection and regulatory forum.
